ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled “temperature (℃)”, with values of about 0, 5, 10, 15; the vertical axis is labeled “height (m)”, with values of about 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000. In the figure there are two line segments a and b in which temperature decreases as height increases; line segment a is located in the lower-height section, and the horizontal difference in temperature changing with height is relatively large; line segment b is located in the higher-height section, and the horizontal temperature difference is relatively small. Then reason: estimated according to the grid, line segment a has a temperature change close to 10℃ within a height difference of about more than 1000 meters, while line segment b has a temperature change of about around 5℃ within a similar height difference, so the magnitude of temperature decrease per unit height of line segment a is larger, that is, the temperature lapse rate is larger. According to geographical laws, dry air or unsaturated moist air has a larger dry adiabatic lapse rate, while saturated moist air, because condensation releases latent heat, has a smaller moist adiabatic lapse rate. Therefore, line segment a, with the larger temperature lapse rate, represents relatively dry air.
